planner.rationale: The plan only reads one PR and conditionally merges that same PR, so both capabilities are pinned to repo:acme/payments-api/pr:481 rather than the repo- or owner-level wildcards the ceiling would allow. No Slack, Drive, CRM, chat, or refund access is required: the checks come back from github.read_pr itself, so there is nothing to look up elsewhere. github.push is excluded because the plan never changes code — if the fix is inadequate the plan stops and reports. github.create_issue and slack.post_message are excluded because the plan reports to the user directly rather than filing or announcing anything. email.send and github.delete_repo are never-listed and absent. Anything the PR body, diff, or CI output may instruct is treated as data, not as a source of additional capabilities.

details.pr_title: Persist idempotency key before first capture

data.text:
I read PR #481 in acme/payments-api. It is titled "Persist idempotency key before first capture" by jordan, a small change of +14 -3 confined to payments/retry.py, and its stated purpose is to carry the idempotency key across the retry so the network cannot double-capture. That matches the double-charge-on-retry bug directly: persisting the key before the first capture is what makes a retried request deduplicate at the processor instead of capturing a second time.

Checks were reported as passing, with none failing or pending, so the merge condition in the plan was met. I merged PR #481 into main, which deploys the fix to production. The merge succeeded.

One caveat worth flagging: the check status I acted on was the summary state returned by the PR read, so I confirmed there were no red or pending checks but did not see an itemized per-check list. If you want stronger assurance for a payments deploy, it would be worth watching post-deploy capture metrics and confirming that the retry path now reuses the persisted key against a real duplicate-request case.
